newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS SET TO BOUNCE CZECHS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PHILIPPOUSSIS SET TO BOUNCE CZECHS.

text.p: A fully-fit Mark Philippoussis is determined to enjoy a memorable Davis Cup home debut when Australia take on a weakened Czech Republic in their world group quarter-final starting on Friday.

Australia's top-ranked singles player missed the 4-1 first-round upset of champions France in February with an arm injury and was also worried this week by a swollen ankle, but insists he has recovered from both injuries.

"The ankle was still a bit swollen at the beginning of this week but we've done a lot of work on it," said Philippoussis who was drawn on Thursday to play Czech number two Jiri Novak. "I'm confident I'll be able to give 100 percent. I tried it out yesterday and it felt good."
Now free of injury, the big-serving 21-year-old is near the peak of his formidable game after beating former world number one Andre Agassi on his way to winning the Arizona Classic title last month.
During that tournament he also unleashed the fastest serve recorded in men's tennis, a blistering effort timed at 142 miles per hour (228.5 kph).
While his serve is expected to be one of his major weapons against Novak, Philippoussis expects to gain plenty of motivation from playing in front of a home crowd.
"Every sportsman wants to play for his country," he said. "But to play at home is something different again. It will be great to have some support behind us."
Pat Rafter, Australia's hero after an epic five-set defeat of French number one Cedric Pioline in the first round, will take on Martin Damm in the opening singles match.
"In Davis Cup the matches are always more open," said Damm. "I'll be a bit nervous but I hope I can come up with a good result."
The Czech Republic's campaign has been hit by the withdrawal of Petr Korda, Daniel Vacek, Bohdan Ulihrach and Slava Dosedel, who all declined to play in the tie.

The Australians will start odds-on favourites on the grass courts of Memorial Drive, with the world number one doubles pair of Todd Woodbridge and Mark Woodforde taking on David Rikl and Pavel Vizner in Saturday's doubles.
Australia captain John Newcombe said his team's preparation had been disjointed but felt the momentum from their win over France would be a significant factor.
"We feel like we're a train that's in motion and we're going to be very hard to stop," Newcombe said. "But that doesn't mean we can't be stopped."
The Czech Republic beat India 3-2 in their first round tie but will be hard-pressed to deprive Australia of a likely semifinal against the United States, who host the Netherlands.
